Two directions can have the same error probabilities whether their errors tend to occur together or in different
states. That distinction determines how often the full report makes at least one error. The example changes
which reversals coincide while holding each domain's distribution and the nine candidate cards fixed.
The joint cap can then change which report has the lowest expected loss among the feasible cards.

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Coincident failures.** The two directions each have error probability 1/10, and they fail together.
  Stating both gives probability 1/10 of at least one error, below the cap 3/20. That card alone minimizes
  expected loss at 1/10.
- **Disjoint failures.** The marginal probabilities remain 1/10, but the probability of at least one error
  rises to 1/5 if the report states both. The cap rules out that card. Two cards tie at risk 7/40, each stating
  one positive direction and withholding the other.
- **Independent domains.** At overlap c=1/100, the probability of at least one error when stating both is 19/100.
  This exceeds the joint cap even under independence, so the same two cards tie for the lowest risk.
- **At the joint cap.** At c=1/20, the probability of at least one error when stating both is exactly 3/20.
  A probability equal to the cap is allowed, so that card is feasible and uniquely optimal.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
The example uses a complete fictional distribution with equal domain weights, withholding cost 1/4, and
zero thresholds. The joint event occurs if either domain's error share exceeds its threshold. A shared
grade leaves a direction unstated. When several feasible cards have the same lowest risk, the app lists all of
them and shows one first. The exact calculation applies to this distribution and these candidates.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="In postrank"}
The [R script](../../data/recipes/profile-dependence.R) reproduces the example with postrank 1.2.0 and gmp.

```r
source("profile-dependence.R")
result <- profile_dependence()
result$summary
```
:::

Source: [postrank multidomain decisions](https://joonho112.github.io/postrank/articles/mdomain-decisions.html).

Standalone: [open this app](../../embed/profile-dependence.html), for example `?preset=coincident&theme=dark`.
